_comment: The servers this repo actually has, one entry each. See SERVERS.md.
There is exactly ONE game entry on purpose. This file previously held five
configurations that each started a vite dev server (dev, dev-alt, dev-alt2,
dev-auto, and rive-test, which was a bare `npx vite`). Every dev server
carries the /__tuning writer from vite.config.js, so a second one is not a
duplicate — any tab still pointed at it can POST its boot-time snapshot over
path/src/imported-tuning.json and silently revert hours of tuning. A picker
with five ways to make that mistake is a trap.
`workbench` is the one to start. It is read-only, it is the index of every
tool in the repo, and it links to whatever else is running - including the
game, whose port it resolves live because vite's port moves every restart.
autoPort where the server honours PORT (vite.config.js and csv-editor.mjs
both do) so two sessions never collide. Fixed 5178 for the workbench: a port
that never moves is the entire point of that one.
The two pickers are fixed-port on purpose and for the opposite reason to
the game: they are read-only render servers that write only their own shots
directory, they cannot touch tuning, and each one owns its port so both can
be up at once. They collide with nothing except a second copy of themselves,
which is what the EADDRINUSE message in atlas-render/server.mjs is for.
